title: Paid Endorsers and Find Your ZYN
lessons: The player asks whether the people they see talking about ZYN online are paid endorsers.
The player notices empty ZYN tins kept and displayed on a windowsill at the rooftop hangout, arranged like a trophy case nobody decided to build.

text: Rooftop, phone out. Someone on your feed is talking about ZYN again. You have started to wonder if he's being paid to.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Is that guy posting about ZYN on my feed paid by you?

entry-first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: I cannot speak to a person I cannot identify. What I can say is that the company's current policy states it does not pay influencers, athletes, or celebrities to endorse the product.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: So all the internet hype is just people doing it themselves?

entry-first-4.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Some of it is people talking on their own. The brand's own pages are limited to platforms with age controls, and the people in its ads are thirty-five or older, by rule. That is what I am permitted to say about the hype.

entry-first-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: This is somehow more legal than saying "no."

entry-first-6.speaker: COUNSEL
text: "No" would have exceeded the available evidence.

choice-first.speaker: COUNSEL
text: You have put the phone face-down. I take that as a prompt.

choices.text: I respect that the brand says it won't pay influencers.
Free hype still does a lot of marketing for you.
I don't want nicotine brands in my social feed either way.

first-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The distinction between paid endorsement and ordinary user speech matters to you. Noted. It matters to me as well, though I am paid to say so.

first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Correct. Nobody paying for it does not mean nobody benefits from it.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Did you just concede a marketing point?

first-2-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: I identified a non-exclusive possibility.

first-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The brand's own accounts are age-gated. Whether you want to see them at all is a separate question, and you are allowed to answer it however you like.
Along the windowsill at the rooftop hangout, a row of empty ZYN tins. Wintergreen, peppermint, cool mint. Nobody remembers deciding to keep them.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Somebody has been keeping every empty tin instead of throwing them out.

entry-return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: No policy requires that. Nothing on the packaging suggests keeping it. The packaging says very little.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the trophy case built itself.

entry-return-4.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Someone decided an empty tin was worth more standing up than in the bin. The company did not design a shelf for that. I checked. I would have liked to find one, for the record. There is not one.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: That is either loyalty or a bad habit wearing a nicer coat.

entry-return-6.speaker: COUNSEL
text: I decline to characterize the coat.

choice-return.speaker: COUNSEL
text: You have counted them. I watched you count them.

choices.text: I'd keep a windowsill like that. It's proof of how long I've been doing something.
Counting a habit in empty tins is still counting.
I don't want a display case tallying how many I've gone through.

return-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Noted. You like a visible record. So do I, professionally. The brand did not have to make this one.

return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Correct. A tin on a windowsill and a tin in a receipt drawer are recording the same thing.

return-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Then throw the empties out as you go. Nothing requires the count to be visible to keep the product.

return-3-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Somewhere a windowsill is disappointed in me.

return-3-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The windowsill has no standing to object.
